decisive_items: a separate cervical os could not be identified and the uterine fundus was not palpable
response.rationale: R2 uniquely explains the inability to identify a separate cervical os and non-palpable uterine fundus, indicating a uterine origin with vaginal extension. Other candidates either lack this specificity (R4, R5, R6, R7, R8) or are contradicted by normal ultrasonography (R3) or non-palpable fundus (R9). R1 (prolapse) is inconsistent with a firm globular mass.

rejected.why: Too generic; does not explain cervical os/fundus findings.
Prolapse would not present as a firm globular mass with inability to identify cervical os.
Vaginal leiomyoma does not explain absent cervical os and non-palpable fundus.
Vaginal cancer is less likely given normal ultrasound and no other signs; lacks specificity.
Sarcoma is rare and not supported by specific findings; same issue as R6.
Contradicted by non-palpable uterine fundus; fibroids would be palpable.
Contradicted by normal pelvic ultrasonography; cervical cancer would likely show abnormality.
Uterine leiomyoma without extension does not explain absent cervical os and vaginal mass.
